\boxed{\dfrac{1}{2t(t-1)}}

**Upper bound.** In a $K_{2,t+1}$-free graph every pair of vertices has at most $t$ common neighbours, so a pair can belong to at most one side of a $K_{t,t}$ (the other side would have to be exactly its common neighbourhood). Each copy of $K_{t,t}$ contains $2\binom t2$ such pairs, and these pairs are distinct across copies. Hence
$$\operatorname{ex}(n,K_{t,t},K_{2,t+1})\le \frac{\binom n2}{2\binom t2}=\frac{n(n-1)}{2t(t-1)}.$$

**Lower bound.** Let $n_e=t^{2e-1}$ and view the vertices as the points of the affine space $\mathrm{AG}(2e-1,\mathbb F_t)$. Its affine lines form a resolvable Steiner system $S(2,t,n_e)$: every pair lies on a unique line of size $t$, and the total number of lines is
$$N=\frac{n_e(n_e-1)}{t(t-1)}.$$
Within each parallel class pair up the lines (at most one line remains unpaired). For each paired pair $(L,L')$ add all $t^2$ edges between $L$ and $L'$. Any two vertices lie on a unique line $L$, so they have exactly the $t$ vertices of the partner line $L'$ as common neighbours; thus the graph is $K_{2,t+1}$-free. Each paired pair gives one copy of $K_{t,t}$, yielding $\lfloor N/2\rfloor$ copies. Therefore
$$\frac{\operatorname{ex}(n_e,K_{t,t},K_{2,t+1})}{n_e^2}\ge \frac{n_e(n_e-1)}{2t(t-1)n_e^2}-o(1).$$

Combining the bounds and letting $e\to\infty$ gives the limit $\displaystyle \frac1{2t(t-1)}$.
